Dormant

/DOR-muhnt/ — rhymes with torment · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Something dormant is temporarily inactive or resting, but still capable of becoming active again later.

The volcano has been dormant for four centuries, quiet but not extinct.

Worked Example

A perennial garden seems dead each winter, but the roots lie dormant beneath the frozen soil, waiting to surge back in spring.

The precise power of dormant is that it means temporary inactivity with the capacity to reawaken—unlike "inactive" or "quiet," which don't promise that return. For a root system, this distinction is crucial: dormant captures both the rest and the future awakening.

How Dormant Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

inactive

Antonyms

How Strong Is It? — resting → sleeping → extinct → dormant

resting vs. dormant

resting vs. dormant: Resting is much milder than dormant: something resting pauses briefly and could stir at any moment, while something dormant has settled into a long, deep inactivity.

sleeping vs. dormant

sleeping vs. dormant: Sleeping is deeper than resting but still weaker than dormant — sleep lasts a night, while a dormant volcano or seed can stay inactive for years or even centuries.

extinct vs. dormant

extinct vs. dormant: Extinct is stronger than dormant and points past it to permanence: a dormant volcano is only temporarily quiet and can still reawaken, but an extinct one is dead forever and will never erupt again.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — dorm-

Root — dorm-: to sleep (Latin dormire) (Latin)

Suffix — -ant

Suffix — -ant: being in a state of (present-participle ending) (Latin, via Old French)

Put it together

Put it together: Dorm- ('to sleep') plus -ant ('in a state of') literally builds 'sleeping.' Something dormant is in a sleeping state — temporarily inactive, but able to wake up and become active again.

Use the root in a new word: dormitory

Use the root in a new word: dormitory: A dormitory is literally a 'place for sleeping' — the same Latin root dormire, 'to sleep,' that makes a dormant volcano one that is merely asleep, not dead.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / scientific

Dormant is technical, used for natural phenomena with the capacity to reawaken—volcanoes, seeds, diseases, seasonal cycles. For human decisions or simple inactivity, 'inactive' or 'paused' is clearer and more natural.
